plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single horizontal strip in which one camera is repeated five times in a row on a white ground, with thick red arrows between and around the copies. Each camera is a black wireframe viewing frustum in three-quarter view: a solid black dot marks the projection center at the left, four straight edges spread rightward from it to the corners of a tall rectangle standing for the image plane, and a faint vertical line inside that rectangle marks its midline. All five frusta match in size and orientation, and every one opens toward the right. A red arrow lies on the axis left of the first camera, another sits in each gap between consecutive cameras, and a final one continues past the last camera to the right edge; all arrowheads point right. Because the arrows run in the same direction the frusta face, the strip shows a camera moving straight ahead down its own optical axis, the case in which the sideways velocity components vanish and only the component along the Z-axis is nonzero.

interactions.label: Animate forward translation
interactions.teaches: The camera advances along its own optical axis while its orientation remains unchanged; in the image this pure forward Z translation appears as radial expansion away from the center

interactions.label: Time along forward path
interactions.teaches: As time increases, scene depth relative to the camera decreases, so projected feature locations move outward from the image center even though there is no sideways camera motion

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The same forward camera translation can be read either as rightward motion of the frustum in 3-D or as an outward optical-flow pattern in the image plane

demo_steps.title: Repeated forward positions
demo_steps.narration: The five identical frusta mark successive camera positions. Every camera opens to the right, and every red arrow points along the same optical axis.

demo_steps.title: Halfway down the optical axis
demo_steps.narration: Scrubbing forward moves the active camera straight right without rotating it. The spacing and orientation show pure Z translation, with no sideways velocity component.

demo_steps.title: Image-plane consequence
demo_steps.narration: Switching to the image plane shows the corresponding optical flow: points move radially outward from the center of expansion as the camera moves forward.

demo_steps.title: Nearer scene, larger flow
demo_steps.narration: Later in the forward path, the outward vectors are longer because the same 3-D forward translation produces larger image displacement as depth decreases.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a long horizontal composition matching the source strip. World-space scale: place five camera centers at x = -4, -2, 0, 2, 4, all on y = 0, z = 0. Each frustum opens toward +X. For each frustum, projection center is a black sphere radius 0.09. Image plane center is about 0.7 units to the right of its projection center. Image-plane rectangle is tall and narrow, approximately 0.55 world units wide in screen/right-depth direction by 1.05 world units tall: corners relative to the plane center approximately (0, ±0.52, ±0.18), giving a slight three-quarter slant. Four black frustum edges run from the center sphere to the four rectangle corners; line width should be visually thick. Draw the image-plane outline in black and the internal vertical midline in gray #777777. Red translation arrows are #ff0000, thick, horizontal, and all point screen-right/+X; place one arrow segment to the left of the first camera, one centered in each gap between cameras, and one extending to the right of the last camera. Arrow shafts should be at the same vertical height as the projection centers. In flow-field mode, use a front-facing square image plane about 3 × 3 units with a black center dot at (0,0). Feature points can be arranged symmetrically around the center, e.g. at normalized image coordinates (±0.35,0), (0,±0.35), (±0.65,±0.35), (±0.35,±0.65), and (±0.8,0). Flow vectors point directly away from the origin with length proportional to radius and to time, using the qualitative forward-motion relation u = -Tz*x/Z, v = -Tz*y/Z; for forward camera motion toward the scene, display outward expansion from the focus of expansion.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the source-like strip as orthographic/axonometric wire geometry with no visible coordinate axes. Keep all five camera copies equal size; do not shrink them with distance. The active camera at the current slider time should be slightly emphasized, for example with a subtle red or orange outline/glow, while the five textbook positions remain as black reference copies. The animation should drive the same timeAlongPath parameter used by the slider. In 3-D strip mode, interpolate the active camera smoothly from the first to the fifth copy along +X while the red arrows remain aligned to +X. In image-plane mode, hide the strip and show a front-on flow field; update vector lengths with time but keep directions radial and centered.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Animation for advancing the camera copies along their optical axis; the frustum moves straight through the scene while projected points expand from the image center, linking forward Z translation to radial optical flow.

discrepancies: The source is a flat horizontal strip of identical camera frusta, but the generated default view shows the strip diagonally in an axonometric 3D view, making the composition substantially different.

The red arrows in the source are large horizontal arrows placed between and outside the camera positions; in the generated figure they are smaller, diagonal in screen space, and appear closer to or passing through the frusta.
An orange highlighted active frustum and faint path line are added, which are not present in the source figure.
The generated code includes an additional image-plane optical-flow mode that is not part of the source figure.
The camera/frustum proportions differ: the generated image planes and frusta look narrower and more compressed than the tall rectangular frusta in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure captures repeated forward camera positions with red motion arrows, but the default diagonal 3D presentation, added orange highlight, and extra flow-field mode reduce visual faithfulness to the simple horizontal source diagram.
action_items: Set the default camera to a flat side-on orthographic view so the frusta and arrows form a horizontal strip matching the source.
Increase the size and screen prominence of the red arrows and place them between camera positions rather than overlapping the frusta.
Remove or hide the orange active-frustum overlay by default to better match the original static figure.
Adjust frustum proportions so the image-plane rectangles are taller and closer to the source line drawing.
plan_action_items: If the goal is strict reproduction of the source figure, omit the separate optical-flow-field mode or make it clearly optional rather than a core part of the planned figure.
